metadata.title: Claude, Is This A Problem.
metadata.topic: IS THIS A PROBLEM · CLAUDE SKILLS FOR LEGAL
metadata.purpose: Answer whether Claude decides 'is this a problem' from its own judgment or from a written specification, using the is-this-a-problem skill's own instruction-set pattern as the concrete case. Lands the carry-out that the skill only checks what its spec defines as a problem — same input, same output, every run, and blind to anything the spec never named.
metadata.anchor_pair: B02 -> B03 (the checklist step: matching a situation against written conditions, reliable when covered, silent when not)

beats.narration_text: Someone assumes Claude judges 'is this a problem' by feel. It doesn't decide — it checks. A written skill spells out exactly what counts as a problem. Liam walks you through it.

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'How does Claude decide if this is a problem?', hesitates on 'decide', corrects to 'check', lands the real question

props.text:
How does Claude decide
if this is a problem?

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('decide' -> 'check') is visible on a late frame.

beats.narration_text: A skill is a folder Claude reads before it acts. This one is called is-this-a-problem. Its SKILL.md holds the whole instruction set, in plain language — no hidden logic, nothing left to guess. Claude reads the file, then follows it. The file is the program.

shot.new_visual_element: A folder opening to reveal one file, SKILL.md, growing into an instruction block

production_viz.label: A folder, then a file
production_viz.mechanic: A folder icon labelled 'is-this-a-problem' opens; inside, one file, 'SKILL.md', slides forward and enlarges into a block of plain-language instruction lines. A small figure glyph labelled 'Claude' reads the block left to right, then a checkmark labelled 'follows it' appears beside the figure.

beats.narration_text: Inside, a Steps section lays out the pipeline: read the situation, check it against a list of defined conditions, then answer. Watch that middle step — the checklist. It isn't Claude weighing the situation on its own; it's Claude matching it against conditions someone already wrote down.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR — a situation flowing through three linear steps: read, check against conditions, answer

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR — read, check, answer
production_viz.mechanic: Three boxes appear left to right, connected by arrows: 'read the situation', 'check against conditions' (this one enlarges and holds, accent border), 'answer'. A situation glyph (a small document icon) travels through all three in sequence, pausing at the middle box while a short list of condition lines fades in beside it. THE ANCHOR. The middle box and its condition list are the composition that returns at B03.

beats.narration_text: Back to that checklist: feed it a situation the list anticipated, and it answers the same way every time — reliable, on repeat. But feed it something the list never named, and it has nothing to fall back on. Not wrong, exactly — just outside what the spec covers. That's the trade a written checklist makes: consistency where it applies, silence everywhere else.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — the same checklist box answering a covered situation the same way three times, then an uncovered situation passing through with no answer

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — reliable, then silent
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 CHECK BOX RETURNS, identical. Three covered-situation glyphs pass through it one after another, each producing the same labelled answer card (teal, 'consistent'). Then a fourth situation glyph, drawn slightly differently (a question-mark texture), passes through the same box; no answer card appears, and a small label reads 'not named — no answer', in terracotta, distinct from a wrong answer.

beats.narration_text: Is this a problem, from Claude, means is this a problem according to the checklist it was given — same input, same output, every run, and only for what that checklist thought to name.

props.quote: Is this a problem, from Claude, means is this a problem according to the checklist it was given — same input, same output, every run, and only for what that checklist thought to name.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. Pick one decision you currently make by gut feel — is this urgent, is this worth escalating, is this a problem. Ask Claude to help you write out the actual criteria you're using as a short checklist, then run your next three real cases through it and flag anything that doesn't fit. Liam, in for Bear.
